newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares open 0.72 percent down.
newsitem.headline: French shares open 0.72 percent down.

text.p: French shares opened 0.72 percent lower on Tuesday in a second day of decline after an unexpectedly strong showing by left-wing parties in the first round of a parliamentary election.
The CAC-40 blue-chip index opened 17 points lower at 2,639, extending Monday's loss of 3.91 percent.
At 0818 GMT, the index had clawed back some of the losses and was down 0.34 percent, or 10.75 points, at 2,643.99 after recovering from a low of 2,641.88. Dealers saw support at 2,640.
They said Alain Juppe's announcement that he would not return as prime minister even if the centre-right won the runoff on June 1 would not help shares.

"Our feeling is that Juppe either resigned too late or too early. It's a joker but it has not been well played," said Olivier Blitz of IFF, adding he saw the CAC-40 sliding to 2,600 before the end of the week.

President Jacques Chirac, who called the snap election on April 21 in a bid to obtain a new centre-right majority during the transition years to European monetary union, will address the nation on television at 1800 GMT on Tuesday night.

"The market could fall to 2,600 before bouncing back because, on the one hand the other European share markets continue to rise, and on the other hand, right or left, it's not the end of the world," a dealer said.
Shares in Thomson-CSF, which fell on Monday on fears its privatisation could be affected by a left wing win, bounced back on Tuesday. At 0857 GMT, they were up 1.58 percent at 174 francs.
Dassault Aviation, suspended on Monday, was twice suspended on Tuesday -- one time limit-down and once limit-up.
Total was 0.74 percent lower at 534 francs. On Monday evening, state agency CDR said it sold 3.5 million shares. Total said it was not the buyer of the 1.4 percent stake.
Elf Aquitaine, unchanged at 597 francs, said it had obtained the exploration licence Very Deep Sea South from the Republic of Congo. The oil group already operates a number of licenses in that area.
